epic.title: Canonical minimal substrate: subject, occupancy episode, holds and jurisdiction across archetypes
epic.description:
Cross-archetype substrate work: the smallest set of subject-agnostic models that lets every archetype run its business, so verticals supply vocabulary and rules rather than cloning structure.

This epic is CROSS-ARCHETYPE and does not overlap EP-5102F494 (animal-welfare vertical) or EP-55AF36AC (veterinary clinic), both of which are archetype-specific and consume what this epic produces.

## Authoritative documents

- `docs/architecture/canonical-minimal-substrate.md` — the element set, what is already built, and sequencing
- `docs/architecture/accommodation-doctrine.md` — how to classify a difference as canonical / vertical / attribute, and the promotion rule
- `docs/architecture/archetypes/pet-rescue-operating-model.md` — discovery probe
- `docs/architecture/archetypes/campground-operating-model.md` — confirmation probe

Specifications should cite these rather than re-deriving the domain.

## State of the substrate (measured 2026-08-25)

Six of nine elements are already canonical, already subject-agnostic, or already designed:

| # | Element | State |
|---|---|---|
| 1-4 | Resource / Availability / CapacityPool / CapacityAllocation | canonical |
| 5 | Staged admission (`CareIntakePacket`) | subject-agnostic since 20260822164000 |
| 6 | Scheduled event (`CareAppointment`) | subject-agnostic since 20260822164000 |
| 7 | **Subject identity** | **missing — keystone** |
| 8 | **Occupancy episode** | clone-only (`HospitalityServiceTurn`) |
| 9 | Episode stage/state + event ledger | already designed (canonical lifecycle grammar + `LifecycleEvent`) |

Promoted by the campground probe under the counting rule, both as extensions of existing designs:

| # | Element | Sightings |
|---|---|---|
| 10 | Concurrent time-bound holds, as a grammar advancement-gate extension | 2 (load-bearing promotes at 2) |
| 11 | Jurisdiction as a rule source, static and dynamic | 2 (load-bearing promotes at 2) |
| — | Resource-to-capability map incl. dimensional fit | 3 (beauty, pet-rescue, campground) |

## Sequencing (dependency, not priority)

1. Canonical subject identity (element 7) — nothing else starts first
2. Occupancy episode (element 8), declaring a lifecycle grammar rather than a new stage enum
3. Animal subject as the first non-patient subject kind — the real test of whether 7 generalised
4. Capability map incl. dimensional fit — lift from `BeautyResourceService`
5. Holds (10) and jurisdiction (11) as extensions, not parallel mechanisms
6. Re-score all three probes

## Method

Promotion uses the `sourceRef` clone-to-canonical backfill pattern already proven by the
hospitality/beauty -> `Resource` migration: add canonical alongside the clone, backfill with a
unique provenance key, dual-read, cut writes, retire. Steps 1-3 are non-breaking, which is what
makes an earlier misclassification cheap to correct.

## Governance question — RESOLVED 2026-08-25

Both triage outcomes were checked and both are correct. No action needed.

- `BI-51C95802` (the ratified direction) was discarded with the reason *"Decision absorbed by
  merged implementation and its remaining animal-identity BI."* Correct — the subject-agnostic
  migration `20260822164000` already shipped, so the decision was executed before it was
  recorded. Its durable home is `docs/architecture/canonical-minimal-substrate.md` and this
  epic, which are better homes than a backlog item for a decision that is not executable work.
- `BI-4F8A484C` (the keystone) was deferred with the reason *"The current AdoptableAnimal
  listing is not an authoritative animal aggregate. A partial model change before reinstall
  would split identity and lifecycle contracts."* Correct, and it sets sequencing: subject
  identity waits for the reset/reinstall cycle rather than landing a partial model change
  against an install about to be torn down.

**Consequence:** step 1 is gated on the next reset cycle, not blocked on a decision.
`BI-2C80E6EA` remains in-progress and owns the vocabulary-layer question; reconcile with it
before writing schema.

items.title: Archetype vocabulary reaches the storefront and nothing else: every consumer lives under storefront/, so a pet rescue's internal cockpit offers Quotes, Orders, Sales Funnel and Invoices to shelter staff
items.body:
## The measurement

Every consumer of archetype vocabulary in the web app:

```
apps/web/app/(shell)/storefront/dispatch/page.tsx
apps/web/app/(shell)/storefront/items/page.tsx
apps/web/app/(shell)/storefront/layout.tsx
apps/web/app/(shell)/storefront/page.tsx
apps/web/app/(shell)/storefront/sections/page.tsx
apps/web/app/(shell)/storefront/setup/page.tsx
apps/web/app/(shell)/storefront/tables/page.tsx
apps/web/app/(shell)/storefront/team/page.tsx
apps/web/app/(shell)/storefront/units/page.tsx
apps/web/app/api/storefront/admin/archetypes/route.ts
apps/web/components/storefront-admin/SetupWizard.tsx
apps/web/app/(shell)/docs/[[...slug]]/page.tsx
```

Search: `customVocabulary|archetypeVocabulary|stakeholderLabel` across `apps/web`.

**Every one is `storefront/`**, plus the docs renderer. Zero consumers in `/workspace`,
`/customer`, `/finance`, `/employee`, `/compliance` — the surfaces the day-to-day operator
actually lives in.

## What that looks like for a shelter

`/customer` on Second Chance Animal Rescue:

> **Customer** · 0 accounts · **+ New Account**
> Nav: Accounts · Engagements · **Pipeline** · **Quotes** · **Orders** · **Sales Funnel** · Marketing
> "No customers are waiting on a reply right now. New bookings and inquiries will appear here first."

A rescue has adopters, applicants, foster families, surrenderers, finders, volunteers and
donors. It has no quotes, no orders, no sales funnel, and no pipeline.

`/finance` is the same story. Vocabulary present: **Invoice, Customer, Revenue**. Vocabulary
absent: **Donation, Donor, Grant, Restricted fund**. The only occurrence of "Animal" anywhere on
that page is the organisation name in the page header — verified by extracting the surrounding
characters, not inferred.

`/compliance` and `/employee` likewise carry no domain vocabulary.

## Why this matters more than wording

**It explains why the archetype looked finished.** All 107 archetypes report
`customVocabulary` populated, and the storefront renders correctly with archetype-appropriate
semantics — Donate rather than Buy, Adopt as Free/Enquire. That is the *only* surface the
vocabulary reaches, and it is the surface an evaluator looks at first. The cockpit behind it is
hardcoded commercial.

**It is a second, distinct defect from BI-2C80E6EA.** That item establishes that
`ArchetypeVocabulary` is eleven labels over one fixed process — a *depth* problem. This is a
*reach* problem: even those eleven labels only reach one surface family. Both must be fixed;
fixing the depth alone would still leave the cockpit saying "Sales Funnel".

**It is a trust problem, not just a usability one.** A shelter worker shown "+ New Account" and
"Quotes" reasonably concludes the product was not built for them. The storefront having the
right words makes it worse, because the inconsistency reads as a demo that was dressed up.

## Suggested fix

1. **Decide the reach contract.** Vocabulary must resolve at the shell/navigation layer, not
   per-page inside one route family, or every new internal surface re-inherits commercial
   defaults by default.
2. **Suppress rather than relabel where the concept does not exist.** A rescue does not need a
   renamed Sales Funnel; it needs no sales funnel. Relabelling "Quotes" to something rescue-ish
   would be worse than hiding it. This is the point at which the depth problem (BI-2C80E6EA)
   and the reach problem meet: reach alone cannot fix a concept that should be absent.
3. **Add a guard.** A ratchet that fails when a shell-level nav label outside `storefront/`
   renders an un-vocabularised commercial term for an archetype whose `customVocabulary`
   defines an alternative. Without one this regresses on the next new route.

## Standing requirement this violates

`docs/architecture/archetypes/pet-rescue-operating-model.md` §7: *"Species-appropriate
vocabulary. A ranch has head of cattle, a shelter has animals in care; neither has 'items'."*
And §5 of the audit method's traps: *"Never accept 'the vocabulary handles it' as evidence of
fit."* — the vocabulary does not even reach the surfaces in question.

Related: `BI-2C80E6EA` (depth, in-progress), `BI-7A38F667` (workspace answers commercial
questions on a shelter). Found during dogfood reset cycle 4.
